title: Differentiation of human monocyte-derived microglia from PBMCs
author: Quek, Cuní-López, et al.
materials: This protocol ensures proper coating of tissue culture plates using Matrigel for successful differentiation of MDMi (https://www.corning.com/catalog/cls/documents/faqs/CLS-DL-CC-026.pdf).14.Thaw Matrigel basement membrane matrix overnight (16–24 h).a.Thaw Matrigel by submerging the vial in ice at 4°C overnight (16–24 h) as per the manufacturer’s recommendation.b.The next day, swirl the Matrigel vial to ensure homogeneity before use.Note: Do not freeze/thaw Matrigel. Instead, aliquot Matrigel and store at −20°C.Note: Matrigel-coated plates are best used the same day, but can be stored in the incubator at 37°C for up to a week in Matrigel coating solution. Do not allow the coated surface to dry out.

steps.title: Obtain permission & prepare reagents
steps.instruction: Confirm institutional approval for work with human samples and prepare all solutions required for monocyte‑derived microglia‑like cell (MDMi) differentiation as listed in the Materials and Equipment section.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs using SepMate‑50 tubes (Protocol I)
steps.instruction: Perform PBMC isolation from 8–9 mL of venous blood using SepMate‑50 tubes and Lymphoprep, keeping all buffers at 23 °C (room temperature).

substeps.instruction: Collect 8–9 mL of blood in K3‑EDTA vacutainer tubes; keep at RT and process within 2 h.
Add 15 mL Lymphoprep to the centre hole of a SepMate‑50 tube; remove any bubbles by pipetting.
Dilute the blood 1:1 with sterile PBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) in a 50 mL Falcon tube; mix gently to homogenise.
Pipette the diluted blood onto the side of the SepMate‑50 tube using the lowest speed setting; the blood should sit above the Lymphoprep.
Centrifuge immediately at 1 200 × g for 10 min at RT with the brake set to maximum.
After centrifugation, if PBMCs adhere to the tube wall, gently dislodge them with a pasture pipette.
Transfer the top (buffy coat) layer to a new 50 mL tube.
Top up the tube with RT sterile PBS containing 1 mM EDTA and resuspend the pellet.
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at RT (23 °C) with brake maximum.
Aspirate supernatant and gently resuspend cells in 1 mL PBS + 1 mM EDTA (visible RBCs may remain).
Remove 10 µL for a Trypan Blue cell count (hemocytometer or automated counter).
Top up the 50 mL tube with PBS + 1 mM EDTA again and centrifuge 300 × g for 10 min at RT.
Aspirate supernatant; the PBMC pellet can be used immediately (see step 21) or cryopreserved.

steps.title: Cryopreserve isolated PBMCs (optional)
steps.instruction: Freeze PBMCs in 10 % DMSO / 90 % cold FBS cryopreservation medium and store first at –80 °C then in liquid‑nitrogen vapor.

substeps.instruction: Prepare cryopreservation medium by mixing 100 µL DMSO with 900 µL cold FBS (FBS must be heat‑inactivated).
Gently resuspend the PBMC pellet in 1 mL of the cryopreservation medium.
Transfer to a pre‑chilled cryovial; label with cell number and date (≈1 × 10⁷ cells per 9 mL blood).
Place the vial in a pre‑chilled Nalgene® Mr. Frosty and store at –80 °C for 24 h.
After 24 h, move vials to the vapor phase of liquid nitrogen.
Do not reuse any unused cryopreservation medium.

steps.title: Isolate PBMCs using density gradient (Protocol II)
steps.instruction: Perform PBMC isolation from 8–9 mL of blood using a Lymphoprep density gradient in standard 50 mL tubes; all buffers at 23 °C.

substeps.instruction: Collect 8–9 mL venous blood in K3‑EDTA tubes; keep at RT and process within 2 h in a biosafety hood.
Mix blood gently, then dilute 1:1 with sterile PBS (no Ca²⁺/Mg²⁺) in a 50 mL Falcon tube.
Add 7.5 mL room‑temperature Lymphoprep to a fresh 50 mL tube.
Layer the diluted blood carefully on top of the Lymphoprep using a transfer pipette; drip against the tube side to avoid mixing.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 30 min at RT (23 °C) with NO brake (deceleration 1/10). If needed, spin an additional 10 min with brake on.
Gently transfer the buffy coat (PBMC layer) to a new 50 mL tube, avoiding Lymphoprep and RBC layers.
Top up with PBS + 1 mM EDTA and centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min (brake on).
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend cells in 1 mL PBS + 1 mM EDTA (RBC contamination may be present).
Remove 10 µL for a Trypan Blue cell count.
Top up the tube with PBS + 1 mM EDTA again and centrifuge 300 × g for 10 min at RT.
Proceed to cryopreservation as described in Protocol I step 7 (or use immediately).
All buffers must be at 23 °C; Lymphoprep may be substituted with Ficoll‑Paque Plus (density 1.077 g/mL).

steps.title: Coat culture plates with Matrigel
steps.instruction: Prepare and apply a 100 µg/mL Matrigel coating on tissue‑culture plates, then incubate overnight.

substeps.instruction: Thaw Matrigel basement membrane matrix on ice at 4 °C for 16–24 h (do not refreeze).
Swirl the vial to ensure homogeneity; keep Matrigel on ice at all times.
Prepare ice‑cold sterile PBS and chill pipette tips by repeatedly pipetting PBS or placing them in the fridge for 10 min.
Spray the ice bucket containing Matrigel with 70 % (v/v) ethanol before placing it in the biosafety hood; work inside the hood.
Dilute Matrigel in ice‑cold PBS to a final concentration of 100 µg/mL (e.g., add 200 µL per cm² of plate surface).
If Matrigel gels in PBS, place the solution at 4 °C for ~10 min until dissolved.
Cover the entire growth surface of the plate with the coating solution, ensuring complete coverage.
Incubate plates at 37 °C/5 % CO₂ overnight (16–24 h).
Do not store unused Matrigel at 4 °C after dilution; aliquot and keep at –20 °C if needed.
Coated plates are best used the same day but can be kept in the incubator (still in coating solution) for up to 1 week; avoid drying out.
Note: Matrigel protein concentration varies 8–12 mg/mL per lot; verify lot concentration if required.
Alternative coating matrix: Geltrex (Thermo Fisher Cat# A1413202).

steps.title: Thaw cryopreserved PBMCs for MDMi differentiation
steps.instruction: Rapidly thaw PBMCs and recover them in pre‑warmed complete RPMI medium while minimising osmotic shock.

substeps.instruction: Prepare complete RPMI medium (heat‑inactivated FBS required) and warm to 37 °C in a water bath.
Remove the PBMC cryovial from liquid nitrogen and thaw in a 37 °C water bath with gentle shaking until a small ice crystal remains.
Wipe the outside of the cryovial with 70 % (v/v) ethanol before moving it into the biosafety hood.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 10 mL tube.
Add pre‑warmed complete RPMI drop‑wise to the tube at a rate of 1 drop per second while swirling, until the volume reaches 4 mL.
Top up the tube to a final volume of 10 mL with pre‑warmed complete RPMI medium (critical to avoid osmotic shock).
Centrifuge the suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at RT (23 °C).
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL pre‑warmed complete RPMI medium.
Take 10 µL for a Trypan Blue cell count; if cells are clumped, pass the suspension through a 70 µm cell strainer.
Proceed to the MDMi differentiation step (step 21).
